rationale: The request adds durable node-result reuse and restart recovery to existing dev_flow and dev_loop workflows. Research must distinguish current flow persistence from operation caching and locate the exact intake, research, and development contracts.

queries.intent: Map the concrete dev_flow and dev_loop package structures before selecting implementation boundaries.
Locate existing cache, checkpoint, resume, and persistence abstractions in flow execution code.
Read the AgentsFlow executor to identify lifecycle hooks and safe cache interception points.
Locate bug intake, research, and development node classes and their result models.
Read dev_flow topology and materialization code to establish node reuse and routing contracts.
Find Redis-backed session and run-state ownership used by dev_loop and dev_flow runners.
Read the existing AgentsFlow persistence specification to preserve established recovery semantics.
Locate tests for flow interruption, resume, idempotency, and repeated node execution.
Identify existing cache contracts elsewhere in the repository that can supply storage and keying patterns.
Inspect recent history for design decisions affecting dev_flow, dev_loop, and AgentsFlow persistence.

expected_findings: Exact node classes and output contracts for bug intake, research, and development
Current distinction between AgentsFlow persistence and dev-loop session/event persistence
Redis ownership and existing serialization conventions
Lifecycle hook suitable for cache lookup and commit-after-success
Required cache identity and invalidation inputs
Existing restart and idempotency test coverage
